name: Sukhothai Kingdom
native: อาณาจักรสุโขทัย (Anachak Sukhothai)

predecessors.name: Khmer Empire
predecessors.text: Sukhothai, which Si Inthrathit's side took out of Khmer vassalage ('the campaign that captured Sukhothai from Khmer vassalage', Ramkhamhaeng page)

successors.name: Ayutthaya Kingdom
successors.text: the Sukhothai core, which Cliopatria transfers to Ayutthaya in 1450 (212 of the 213 cells Ayutthaya gains lie in Sukhothai's 1449 shape)

ledger.x: 1238: Si Inthrathit founds the kingdom of Sukhothai.
1279: Ram Khamhaeng's reign opens and the kingdom grows beyond its core.
By 1287: Ram Khamhaeng recognises Wareru of Martaban as a vassal.
The southern peninsula joins Ram Khamhaeng's greatest extent.
Phrae and Muang Sua pay tribute to Ram Khamhaeng.
The uplands north and east of the Sukhothai plain join the greatest extent.
1298: Ram Khamhaeng dies and the northern tributaries break away.

c. 1299: the northern dominions break away. Sukhothai page: 'The tributaries fell away quickly after his death' (Ram Khamhaeng, 1298); 'The dominions north of Uttaradit, among them the Lao kingdoms of Muang Sua and Vieng Chan Vieng Kham ... broke free'. Lan Xang page: after Ram Khamhaeng's death 'both Vieng Chan Vieng…

c. 1300: the peninsula leaves. Sukhothai page: 'To the south, Suphannaphum Kingdom and Nakhon Si Thammarat left early in Loe Thai's reign'. Loe Thai reigned 1298-1323 (Loe Thai page, lead and infobox), so 'early' is a window of the first years and 1300 is my bridge inside it. Review fix: replaces the 1375 loss to…

c. 1300: Suphannaphum leaves. Sukhothai page: 'Suphannaphum Kingdom ... left early in Loe Thai's reign'; Loe Thai page: Suphan Buri 'also broke free early in the reign of Loe Thai' (summary; the page names Suphan Buri, not Suphannaphum). The page names only Suphannaphum; the region is the rest of the 1363 outline…
1363: Lithai moves the capital of Sukhothai to Phitsanulok.
1438: Ayutthaya takes Sukhothai in a personal union.
1438: Sukhothai ends as an independent kingdom.

wars.name: Ayutthaya's invasion of Sukhothai of 1349
wars.outcome: Ayutthayan armies 'invaded and made Sukhothai a tributary'.

wars.name: Lan Xang-Sukhothai war of the 1360s
wars.outcome: 'Fa Ngum again led Lan Xang to war in the 1360s against Sukhothai', in which Lan Xang 'was victorious in defense of their territory'; no land changes hands on the page.

wars.name: Ayutthayan subjugation of Sukhothai (1378 and 1438)
wars.outcome: 'In 1378 Lue Thai submitted as a vassal'; in 1438 an Ayutthayan garrison 'ended Sukhothai's independence'.

certainty.note: A mandala of city-states: the page says 'kingdoms such as Sukhothai lacked distinct borders'; no frontier of this state is fixed by treaty or survey.
